note: Every source below was opened and read in this session. 'read' means the page was fetched and the value attributed to it was taken from that page. 'not-read' sources are registered as the designated authority for a future capture but nothing on this site is attributed to them.

sources.name: Official NFL Injury Report - Week 10, 2026
sources.verifies: data/lab/injuries_week10_2026.json - 347 rows across 28 clubs, transcribed verbatim
sources.caveat: A live document. It reflects the league's filings as published at the capture time; a capture on a different day of the same game week will legitimately differ.

sources.name: Official NFL 2026 schedule, by week (weeks 1-10)
sources.chunks_read: 20 of 20 (2 chunks per week x 10 weeks)
sources.verifies: data/lab/results_2026.json - every game the official page marks FINAL, with date, clubs and final score
sources.caveat: Two Week 10 games were not FINAL at capture time and are stored with null scores.

sources.name: Official NFL game centre, Week 10 (14 fixtures)
sources.chunks_read: 1 of 2-3 per game; the 'Game Info' panel is in chunk 0
sources.verifies: data/lab/fixtures_week10_2026.json - Location, Stadium and the official Game Book PDF link per fixture
sources.caveat: The game centre's pre-game injury cards use coarser practice wording than the injury report; the injury report wins.

sources.name: NFL.com Terms and Conditions
sources.chunks_read: 1 of 9 (section 1 read in full; section 1.3 is the binding clause quoted on this site)
sources.verifies: The legal constraint on the price-data policy and on the public/private data split: section 1.3 permits use 'solely for your own individual non-commercial and informational purposes' and prohibits 'systematic retrieval of data or other content ... whether to create or compile, directly or indirectly, a collection, compilation, database, or directory ... absent our express prior written consent'. Page header reads 'Updated: May 16, 2024'.
sources.caveat: Not legal advice. Sections 15-18 (warranties, liability, arbitration) were not read in this session and are not characterised here.

sources.name: 2026 NFL Rulebook (NFL Football Operations)
sources.chunks_read: 1 of 3 (the '2026 Rule Changes' table read in full)
sources.verifies: The four 2026 rule changes, quoted verbatim, including rule 6-1-6 which 'Permits the kicking team to declare an onside kick at any time during the game' - the official basis for the kickoff/onside-kick regime prior.
sources.caveat: No rule-derived numeric model value is inferred from this page.

sources.name: Official NFL Game Books (PDF, published per game in the game centre)
sources.chunks_read: 0 - the PDF links were read off the official game centre pages; no PDF was parsed in this session
sources.verifies: That an official Game Book exists for 12 of the 14 Week 10 fixtures. The links are published on the Fixtures page so actual starters and game-day status can be transcribed from the authoritative source rather than inferred.
sources.caveat: No starter, snap count or inactive list has been transcribed yet. Those columns are blank and flagged.

sources.name: NFL Next Gen Stats (NFL Football Operations)
sources.caveat: Registered as the candidate official source for tracking-derived context features. No statement is made about whether raw tracking data is public or licensed.

sources.name: National Weather Service (NOAA) - official US government weather source
sources.caveat: Designated as the official source for the stadium roof/surface and hourly wind/precipitation overlay. No forecast, wind speed or precipitation value appears anywhere on this site.

sources.name: NFL flexible scheduling procedures (published with the schedule)
sources.caveat: Linked from the official schedule page as the authority for late-season date/time changes. Relevant to the fixture-context feature set; unread, so no claim is made.

sources.name: scikit-learn - Brier score loss
sources.caveat: Method reference only. Registered by an earlier session; this session does not restate any formula detail from it.

sources.name: scikit-learn - TimeSeriesSplit
sources.caveat: Method reference only, for the chronological train/validation/holdout design. No numeric claim.

sources.name: This repository on GitHub (commit history used for the repo review)
sources.chunks_read: git log / ls-tree / REST API, not page chunks
sources.verifies: data/lab/repo_review.json - commit hashes, file inventory and Pages configuration
